Compute Transcription Factor (TF) activity

compute.TFs.activity.Rd

Infers transcription factor (TF) activity from a gene expression matrix with decoupleR::decouple() (Badia-i-Mompel et al., 2022). By default the univariate linear model ("ulm") is used. The TF-target network can be provided by the user, obtained from prebuilt collections (CollecTRI from OmnipathR or Dorothea from the dorothea package), or read from an ARACNe-inferred network.

Usage

compute.TFs.activity(
  counts_norm,
  TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
  min_targets_size = 5,
  universe = NULL,
  cancer_type = NULL,
  method = "ulm",
  scale = TRUE,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = NULL
)

Arguments

counts_norm

A gene expression matrix with genes (symbols) as rows and samples as columns, with unique sample names. The matrix should be log-normalized (e.g., log2(TPM + 1), log2CPM, etc.). A warning is given if it has values above 20, which log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.

TF.collection

Character. The source of the TF-target network. Options are "CollecTRI" (default), "Dorothea", or "ARACNE".

  • "CollecTRI" uses the prebuilt collection from OmnipathR and "Dorothea" (confidence A and B) the one from the dorothea package. Each collection is cached in its own file, Results/TF_target_collection_<TF.collection>.csv, and reused on later calls: a message gives the number of TFs and interactions of the cached file and the date it was saved. A cached file that is empty or lacks the columns source, target and mor is not used (the collection is obtained again, with a warning). Delete the file to obtain the collection again.

  • "ARACNE" reads a tab-separated network file with Regulator and Target columns from input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt (relative to the working directory). The mode of regulation of each edge is read from a mor column of the file (1 activation, -1 repression), which should be the sign of the Spearman correlation between TF and target computed on the cohort used to build the network. If the file has no mor column, a warning is given and the signs are computed as the sign of the Spearman correlation between TF and target in the samples of counts_norm; they then depend on the samples given (e.g. they can differ between cohorts, or between a training and a test set).

min_targets_size

Integer. Minimum number of target genes per regulon (passed to decoupleR::decouple() as minsize). Default is 5.

universe

Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target interactions (columns source, target, mor). The three columns are required: mor is the mode of regulation (1 activation, -1 repression; use 1 for every edge if the network has no sign). If not provided, the network is fetched based on TF.collection. Ignored when TF.collection = "ARACNE".

cancer_type

Optional character. TCGA cancer type abbreviation used to locate the ARACNe network (only used when TF.collection = "ARACNE"). If NULL, the network is auto-detected when only one network.txt exists under input/ARACNE/.

method

Character. The decoupleR statistic used to score the TFs: "ulm" (univariate linear model, default), "mlm" (multivariate linear model), "wsum" (weighted sum) or "consensus" (consensus of the three).

scale

Logical. If TRUE (default), z-score scales the TF activity matrix across samples. The scaled scores of a sample then depend on the other samples given in the same call; use scale = FALSE to get scores that can be compared between separate calls (e.g. a training and a test set). With fewer than three samples the scores are not scaled (a message is given).

return

Logical; if TRUE, saves matrix in Results/ folder. Default is TRUE.

file_name

Optional character suffix used when writing the TF activity matrix to disk (Results/TF_matrix_<file_name>.csv; without it, Results/TF_matrix.csv).

Value

A data frame of inferred (and, if scale = TRUE, scaled) TF activity scores, with samples as rows and TFs as columns. Column names are made syntactically valid with make.names() (e.g. NKX2.1), in the returned table and in the saved file.

References

Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of computational methods to infer biological activities from omics data. Bioinformatics Advances, 2(1), vbac016. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

Tuerei, D., Korcsmaros, T., & Saez-Rodriguez, J. (2016). OmniPath: guidelines and gateway for literature-curated signaling pathway resources. Nature Methods, 13(12), 966-967. https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4077

Garcia-Alonso, L. et al. (2019). Benchmark and integration of resources for the estimation of human transcription factor activities. Genome Research. https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.240663.118

Lachmann, A. et al. (2016). ARACNe-AP: gene network reverse engineering through adaptive partitioning inference of mutual information. Bioinformatics, 32(14), 2233-2235. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw216

Margolin, A.A. et al. (2006). ARACNE: an algorithm for the reconstruction of gene regulatory networks in a mammalian cellular context. BMC Bioinformatics, 7(Suppl 1), S7. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-7-S1-S7

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Downloads the CollecTRI network from OmniPath
data("counts.norm.tuto")
tfs_activity <- compute.TFs.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
} # }
